sentences.text:
The appellant has been arrested on 01.10.2024 in connection with Crime No.766/2024 registered at Police Station Manawar, District Dhar (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n)
& 506 of IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31875 2 CRA-12085-2024 (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.
As per the case of prosecution, prosecutrix aged around 21 years reported to SHO, P.S. Manawar Distt. Dhar on 29.09.2024 that she is studying in Class XII.
She got friendly with Rahul Dodwe at Mauj Masti Coffee House.
Rahul had physical relations with her at his rented room between January, 2024 to August, 2024 on the pretext of marriage.
When she asked Rahul to marry her, he refused to marry and threatened to kill her.
She informed her parents and came to report the matter.

On such allegations, P.S. Manawar, Distt. Dhar registered FIR bearing Crime No. 766/2024 for offences punishable u/Ss 376, 376(2)(n),& 506 of IPC and Section, 3(2)(v) of Scheduled Castes Rahul vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147414597/
1 and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act against Rahul Dodwe(Applicant).
Prosecutrix was forwarded for medico legal examination.
She informed the Medical Officer that she was residing with Rahul in Live-in-relationship.
When she asked Rahul to marry her, he threatened to kill her.
The statements of prosecutrix were recorded u/S 180 and 183 BNS, 2023.
She made similar allegations against Rahul.
Appellant - Rahul Dodwe was arrested on 01.10.2024
He is in custody ever since.
Relevant seizures have been made.
Investigation is almost complete.
Learned Counsel for the appellant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in this matter.
It is a case of consensual relationship between two educated adults.
When their relationship turned sour and could not culminate into marriage, false allegations of rape have been levelled against the appellant.
The appellant is aged around 19 years.
There is no likelihood of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31875 3 CRA-12085-2024 his absconsion leaving his family, home and job.
No custodial interrogation of the appellant is needed in the matter.
There is no likelihood of his tampering with evidence by the appellant.
The trial would take time to conclude.
Learned trial Court has committed an error in rejecting the bail application of the appellant under Section 483 of BNSS.
Therefore, the appellant may be extended the benefit of bail.
Per contra, learned Counsel for the State ably assisted by learned counsel for the objector/complainant opposes the appeal on the ground of gravity of offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, while setting aside order dated 21.10.2024 passed by Trial Court, this Court is inclined to release the appellant on bail.
Thus, the appeal is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that appellant - Rahul S/o Ramesh Dodwe shall be released on bail in connection with Crime No.766/2024 registered at Police Station Manasa District Dhar (M.P.) for offences punishable under Section(s) 376, 376(2)(n), & 506 of IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rs.
